producer_report.summary: I restored the rules the first trim dropped and pinned them in tests. The verifier frame has its cited-document rule again, with request_reading_mismatch. It also has 'Judge user-facing output as its audience would', 'personal data' in the harms list, a stated absence-is-not-a-finding line, and 'Change nothing.' The reader has its producer_model guidance back. The planner has its revision rule back, in shorter words. All of these are phrases in FRAME_ANCHORS in lib.rs. The contract-size test is an exact assert_eq! again, on 929 bytes. docs/agent-reference.md now says the rules are stated in the prompt or the brief. docs/system-facts.md has the new budget lines (reader 1929, verifier 1233, planner 1105), which a test forces. The CHANGELOG has the measured counts, and I dropped its claim that every set sits under 90% of its budget; the lib.rs comment I dropped too. D168 in docs/decisions.md lists each passage still removed, by file, with its reason. I ran the athena-context, budgets, mirrors and policy tests; all pass. clippy and the full suite are left to Athena.

open_issues: D168's relocation list is written by hand. No code compares old and new prompt rules.
The planner frame is near its 800-token bound, and the verifier set has 67 tokens of headroom.
mistakes: The first trim's comment and CHANGELOG claimed the largest sets were at or under 90% of their budgets. After restoring the rules the verifier set is 1233 of 1300 and the planner 1105 of 1200, so I removed that claim.
learnings: The system_facts test pins budget lines to computed sizes, so every prompt edit means updating docs/system-facts.md.
The planner frame test bound is 800 tokens; the restored revision rule had to be shortened to fit.
